To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the regulation of body temperature by the nervous system involves a complex network of molecular and neural circuits that sense temperature and integrate this information to generate appropriate behavioral and physiological responses.
the hypothalamus is the center for thermoregulation, and that the thermoregulatory circuits in this region are organized in a manner that is consistent with the thermoregulation model of B. L. King.

(1) The hypothalamus is the central integrator of thermoregulations, (2) Thermosensitive neurons in the hypothalamus receive information about core temperature from thermoreceptors in the skin, and (3) The hypothalamically generated thermoregulatory response involves the coordinated activation of the sympathetic nervous system and the endocrine system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural basis for thermoregulation.
the molecular, cellular and systems level mechanisms of thermoregulated behavior in mammals.
the neural control of body temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the regulation of body temperature by the nervous system is a very complicated process.
the regulation of body temperature by the nervous system is a complex, multi-faceted and highly integrated process that is still poorly understood at the cellular and molecular level.
the nervous system is a complex system that regulates the body temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the regulation of body temperature by the nervous system is a complex process that involves the integration of multiple sensory modalities.
we are still in the dark about the molecular mechanisms of thermosensation and thermoregulation.
the brain is the most important organ for the body temperature regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermoregulatory circuits are highly conserved across species, and that the molecular and cellular components of these circuits are likely to be similar across mammals.

the thermoregulatory system is highly complex and that it is likely that the brain has evolved multiple parallel pathways for the detection of temperature changes in different body compartments and the integration of these inputs to coordinate a homeostatic response.

the thermoregulatory system is highly integrated with many other physiological systems, including the cardiovascular system, and that the nervous system plays a central role in coordinating the homeostatic responses that are required to maintain body temperature within a narrow range.
